issues.description: The template, problem statement, and REST resource expect PersonService.addChild to be called with signature addChild(Person person, Person child) where the first parameter is the parent (person) and the second is the child. In the solution the implemented method uses the same compiled signature (two Person parameters) but the parameter order/semantics in the implementation are swapped (method declared as addChild(Person child, Person person) and the implementation treats the first parameter as the child). This results in the service logic operating on the wrong argument positions when invoked by PersonResource (which calls addChild(person, persistedChild)), causing incorrect behavior and confusion when comparing template/specification to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution implementation align with the template/specification: declare and implement addChild as addChild(Person person, Person child) (first parameter = parent, second = child). Inside the method, check the child's parents (child.getParents()) and add the child to the parent's children set (person.getChildren().add(child)), then save and return the parent via personRepository.save(person). Ensure parameter names and internal logic match the intended semantics so PersonResource.addChild(person, persistedChild) behaves correctly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template define the addChild method as addChild(Person person, Person child) (parent first, child second). In the solution, the addChild method signature is implemented as addChild(Person child, Person person) (parameters reversed). This parameter-order/name mismatch across artifacts creates a conceptual mapping barrier: students reading the problem and template expect to call addChild(parent, child), while the solution's implementation treats the first argument as the child and the second as the parent, which is confusing and can lead to incorrect reasoning about which object is modified and saved.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's addChild signature and implementation match the problem statement and template: change the solution method to public Person addChild(Person person, Person child) and implement it so it checks child.getParents().size() < 2, adds child to person's children set (person.getChildren().add(child)), and saves/returns the parent (person) via personRepository.save(person).
